h: Hormone-sensitive lipase in adipocytes: stimulated by which hormone?
p: Catecholamines (via beta receptors, cAMP and PKA) activate hormone-sensitive lipase to release fatty acids and glycerol; insulin inhibits it.

h: Chronic productive cough in a smoker with cardiomegaly: pulmonary vascular change?
p: Chronic hypoxia causes pulmonary vasoconstriction and remodeling, raising pulmonary vascular resistance and leading to cor pulmonale.

h: ASC-US with negative HPV test: repeat cotesting in?
p: Per ASCCP/USPSTF cervical screening guidance, HPV-negative ASC-US returns to routine screening (cotesting at 3 years). HPV-positive ASC-US goes to colposcopy. Guidelines are updated periodically.

h: Neuromuscular junction: presynaptic Ca2+ influx triggers what?
d: Generation of the end plate potential
Release of Ca2+ into the synaptic cleft
p: Voltage-gated Ca2+ entry causes SNARE-mediated vesicle fusion and ACh release; ACh then binds nicotinic receptors to produce the end plate potential.

h: Preeclampsia IV drug causing headache, tachycardia, edema: its mechanism?
p: Hydralazine dilates arterioles, triggering reflex tachycardia and fluid retention, with headache and flushing; lupus-like syndrome with chronic use.

h: Delusions and flat affect for 3 months: diagnosis?
p: Schizophreniform lasts 1-6 months; brief psychotic disorder is under 1 month; schizophrenia needs 6 months or more.

h: Tender blue-red subungual papule, pain with cold: tumor of which cells?
p: Glomus tumors arise from glomus body cells (modified smooth muscle) controlling temperature regulation, and are exquisitely tender and cold-sensitive.

h: Sublingual nitroglycerin for angina: main site of action?
p: Nitrates mainly dilate veins, reducing preload and myocardial oxygen demand; NO release raises cGMP in smooth muscle.

h: Neostigmine reversal of a nondepolarizing blocker: give with which drug?
p: Neostigmine raises ACh at muscarinic sites too, causing bradycardia and secretions; an antimuscarinic prevents these effects.

h: Fever, rash, eosinophiluria after NSAID: biopsy finding?
p: Acute interstitial nephritis is a type IV hypersensitivity to drugs (NSAIDs, penicillins, PPIs, sulfonamides); stop the offending drug, steroids if severe.

h: ALS (upper and lower motor neuron loss): disease-slowing drug?
p: Riluzole reduces glutamate excitotoxicity and modestly prolongs survival. Nusinersen treats spinal muscular atrophy; glatiramer treats multiple sclerosis.

h: Male pattern baldness drug that lowers libido: mechanism?
p: Finasteride blocks conversion of testosterone to DHT; side effects are decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. Also used for BPH.

h: Second pharyngeal pouch gives rise to which structure?
p: Pouch 1: middle ear, Eustachian tube. Pouch 2: palatine tonsil. Pouch 3: thymus and inferior parathyroids. Pouch 4: superior parathyroids.

h: Hyperphagia, obesity, hypogonadism, almond-shaped eyes: genetic mechanism?
a: Silencing of the maternal chromosome 15 copy (paternal 15q11-13 lost)
p: Prader-Willi: loss of paternal 15q11-q13 genes (deletion or maternal uniparental disomy) because the maternal copy is imprinted/methylated; Angelman is the maternal-deletion counterpart.

h: Cuboidal epithelium, smooth muscle, no cartilage or goblet cells: airway segment?
p: Terminal bronchioles end the conducting zone: ciliated cuboidal cells with club cells, smooth muscle, no cartilage or goblet cells. Respiratory bronchioles have alveolar outpouchings.

h: Chocolate-colored blood, cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen: antidote?
p: Methemoglobinemia (Fe3+ hemoglobin; triggered by drugs such as dapsone, nitrates, benzocaine) is treated with methylene blue, which reduces Fe3+ to Fe2+.

h: Hypotension, distant heart sounds, JVD, fluid-unresponsive: ECG sign?
d: Wide QRS complexes without P waves
p: Cardiac tamponade (Beck triad): the heart swings in a pericardial effusion, producing electrical alternans and low voltage; treat with pericardiocentesis.

h: Intraoperative hypercarbia, tachycardia, hyperthermia after anesthesia: treatment?
p: Malignant hyperthermia (volatile anesthetics, succinylcholine; RYR1 mutation) is treated with dantrolene, which blocks sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release.

h: Neonate with high ammonia, high orotic acid, low citrulline: treatment?
p: OTC deficiency (X-linked) blocks the urea cycle: ammonia and orotic acid rise with low citrulline. Treat with sodium benzoate/phenylacetate, protein restriction, arginine or citrulline.

h: HIV with CD4 of 162: which prophylaxis?
p: Start TMP-SMX when CD4 falls below 200. Toxoplasma prophylaxis begins below 100 (if IgG positive).

h: Droplike scaly papules after strep pharyngitis: diagnosis?
p: Guttate psoriasis classically follows streptococcal infection in young patients and often resolves spontaneously.

h: Child with GM2 ganglioside accumulation and neurodegeneration: missing enzyme?
p: Tay-Sachs disease (hexosaminidase A deficiency): cherry-red macula, hypotonia, neurodegeneration, no hepatosplenomegaly. Sandhoff lacks both A and B.

h: c-ANCA (anti-proteinase 3): associated vasculitis?
p: GPA: upper airway (nasal ulcers, sinusitis), lung nodules and glomerulonephritis. p-ANCA (MPO) is seen in microangiitis and eosinophilic GPA.

h: Cocaine withdrawal: expected symptom?
p: Stimulant crash brings fatigue, hypersomnia, depression and hyperphagia, unlike opioid withdrawal (lacrimation, diarrhea) or alcohol/benzodiazepine withdrawal (seizures).
